exposure: Elective induction at 39 weeks vs. expectant management
cohort: 115,502 mother-infant dyads who delivered at 25 hospitals between 2008 and 2011. This analysis included low-risk parous women with nonanomalous singletons with at least one prior vaginal delivery after 20 weeks, who delivered at ≥39(0/7) weeks
finding: Elective induction of labor at 39 weeks was associated with decreased odds of cesarean delivery and maternal morbidity, without an increase in neonatal adverse outcomes in low-risk parous women.
mod_finding: In low-risk parous women, elective induction of labor at 39 weeks was associated with decreased odds of cesarean delivery and maternal morbidity.
